text:
sam.k: Hey team — first day trying to get the local stack running. Postgres container comes up but my Rails app keeps throwing `PG::ConnectionBad: could not connect to server: No such file or directory`. I'm on a Mac (M1) using Docker Desktop. Compose snippet below. Anyone know if this is a unix socket vs TCP host issue? @alice.devex

alice.devex: Are you connecting from the host machine or from another container? That determines whether you should use localhost/127.0.0.1 (TCP) or a unix socket / service name.

sam.k: I'm running `rails s` on my host (not in a container) and DB is in docker-compose. My DATABASE_URL is `postgres://postgres:pass@localhost:5432/app_dev`. Weirdly `psql -h localhost -U postgres` succeeds, but Rails still complains. Paste of the Rails stack trace: `PG::ConnectionBad: could not connect to server: No such file or directory - Is the server running locally and accepting connections?`

alice.devex: A couple of things to check quickly: 1) Make sure your postgres service in compose has `ports: - \"5432:5432\"` so the container port is exposed to the host. 2) If libpq is trying a socket, ensure your DATABASE_URL/PGHOST is set (explicitly use 127.0.0.1 not unix socket). On mac, `localhost` usually resolves to host, but some drivers fall back to sockets if host is nil. Try `PGHOST=127.0.0.1 rails c`.

ben.infra: Also run `docker-compose logs postgres` to see if Postgres actually reports it is listening on 0.0.0.0:5432 or if it failed to initialize due to volume permission issues (common when mounting host dir).

sam.k: Good call. My compose has this section:
```
services:
  postgres:
    image: postgres:14
    volumes:
      - ./tmp/postgres:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    ports:
      - "5432:5432"
    environment:
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: pass
```
I did `docker-compose up -d` and saw the container restart a couple times. Logs showed `could not change permissions of /var/lib/postgresql/data: Permission denied`.

infra-bot: [alert] postgres restarted 3 times in the last 5 minutes (container postgres).

ben.infra: Yep that's the ownership issue. If you mount a host folder, chown it to the postgres uid before starting: `sudo chown -R 999:999 ./tmp/postgres` then `docker-compose down && docker-compose up -d`. Alternatively remove the bind mount to let the image manage the volume.

sam.k: I ran `sudo chown -R 999:999 ./tmp/postgres` and recreated the container. `docker-compose logs postgres` now shows `database system is ready to accept connections`. After that `PGHOST=127.0.0.1 rails db:migrate` works and the Rails app boots. Thanks! :tada: 

ben.infra: Nice. Short tips to remember: - app running on host -> use 127.0.0.1 and ensure ports mapped. - app in container -> use service name (postgres) as host and the internal Docker network. - For Mac M1, prefer official images with arm64 support if you see architecture errors.

sam.k: Quick follow-up — Redis was also in compose but my app said `ECONNREFUSED`. Fixed by setting `REDIS_URL=redis://127.0.0.1:6379/0` and exposing the port in compose. All green now.

alice.devex: Sweet. If you plan to run both app+db in containers, we have a `stack-local` compose template in the repo that wires service names and networks — ping me and I can point you to it. Welcome aboard! :rocket: 

devops: If you hit permission problems often, we have a small README in infra/dev-local about recommended UID/GID and using named volumes instead of bind mounts on mac.

sam.k: Will do. Thanks everyone!
